cands.name: Adline C. Clarke

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Democratic member of the Alabama House for District 97 (Mobile) since winning a May 2013 special election. Former Mobile Press-Register reporter and editor, bookstore and staffing-service owner, and communications officer and senior vice president at Mobile Development Enterprises.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as recommended by two Sway voting groups: 'Rhythm, Beats, and Ballots - Mobile' and 'The Neighborhood Guy's Candidates Jamboree'.

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions or actions from Clarke on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, police and public order, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. Her campaign site lists 2026 priorities of health care, voting access, childcare, transportation and job training. Ballotpedia says she did not complete its 2026 or 2022 candidate surveys. Her birthplace and where she grew up are not stated in the pages we read. The roots score is based on her Mobile schooling and long residence, not on a stated birthplace. No news reports on controversies or foreign ties were available.

local.label: Roots 90: Her campaign site says she graduated from Davidson High School and Spring Hill College, both in Mobile, and that she is a life-long member of St. James Major Catholic Church. Her birthplace is not stated in the pages reviewed. · Money: 1% of money from District 97 ZIP codes

qual.background: Alabama House member since 2013 (13 years). Earlier worked 15 years at the Mobile Press-Register, rising to its first female City Editor, then ran a bookstore and a staffing business and held a senior role at Mobile Development Enterprises.
qual.why: More than a decade of legislative service puts her in the high band. She has also run businesses and worked in public administration. Her page does not say she held chamber leadership.
